evidence_rule: Material measurements are comparators under their own conditions. None validates a living, growing, self-repairing lunar floater. Missing temperature, humidity, thickness or aging evidence is not silently supplied.

sources.title: Evaluation of Hydrogen Permeability of Polymer Membranes
sources.access: Publisher abstract read; linked full PDF timed out.
sources.measurement: Room-temperature H2 permeability; cellophane 5.78e-17 and polypropylene 2.24e-15 mol m/(m2 s Pa).
sources.conditions: Room temperature; precise temperature, humidity, sample thickness and aging not recovered from abstract.
sources.limitation: The paper reports thickness dependence for some tested polymers. Constant-P thickness scans are conditional extrapolations.

sources.title: Permeability of Synthetic Film-forming Materials to Hydrogen
sources.report: NBS Research Paper RP750; Journal of Research NBS 13, 879-885
sources.access: Official seven-page PDF read; Table 2 visually checked.
sources.conditions: 25 C; air opposite hydrogen at 30 mm water gauge. The 65% RH/70 F condition concerns specimen weighing, not verified gas-test humidity.
sources.limitation: Liter reference state not explicit in inspected passage; retain reported transmission rather than claiming an exact intrinsic permeability.

sources.title: Balloon Fabrics Made of Goldbeater's Skins
sources.report: NACA Technical Memorandum 172; translation of L'Aeronautique, August 1922
sources.access: Official NASA/NACA full PDF read, especially printed page 11.
sources.transmission: Qualitative few liters H2 per m2 per day at 30 mm water gauge; not a precise numeric coefficient.
sources.construction: Processed intestinal membranes, crossed layers, cotton, glue and varnish; gas cells generally protected inside rigid airships.
sources.limitation: Historical manufactured animal-derived barrier; no living tissue, autonomous repair, modern humidity sweep or quantified service-life evidence.

sources.title: Spray deposition of sulfonated cellulose nanofibers as electrolyte membranes in fuel cells
sources.access: Full publisher HTML, methods and results read.
sources.conditions: In-situ hydrogen/nitrogen LSV; crossover current at 300 mV; humid 80 C fuel-cell configuration. Separate dry permeation testing is not the humid measurement.
sources.limitation: A device flux, not an intrinsic room-temperature permeability. Thin spray film exhibited cracks/pinholes. Durability demonstration was short, not multiyear.

sources.title: Lignin-Rich Microfibrillated Cellulose: A Sustainable Alternative for Proton Exchange Membranes for Energy Applications
sources.access: Primary publisher indexed excerpts only; direct full-text access failed.
sources.conditions: Reported room temperature; comparable film thicknesses 17.3-18.7 micrometers in indexed results. H2-test humidity and precise procedure not verified.
sources.limitation: Conditions-incomplete sensitivity only. Do not import conductivity-test humidity into the H2 measurement.

sources.title: Extraction of Chitin Nanofibers and Utilization for Sustainable Composites and Foams
sources.publication: Georgia Institute of Technology doctoral thesis, Table 2.3
sources.access: Official thesis indexed table excerpt recovered; PDF initially opened but subsequent page retrieval blocked. Full methods not verified.
sources.related_article_title: Facile Route to Produce Chitin Nanofibers as Precursors for Flexible and Transparent Gas Barrier Materials
sources.conditions: Temperature, relative humidity, thickness and aging not established from accessible table excerpt.
sources.limitation: Low-P sensitivity with incomplete conditions, not an admitted wet-flight material or quantitative living-membrane prediction.

sources.title: Gas permeability of a novel cellulose membrane
sources.relevance: Dry and water-swollen cellulose studied with H2 among several gases, 298-353 K and pressures up to 1 MPa.
sources.limitation: No numeric swollen-state H2 coefficient recovered; no wet multiplier used.

sources.title: Antioxidant and UV-Blocking Leather-Inspired Nanocellulose-Based Films with High Wet Strength
sources.access: Primary full-text measurement reviewed by the mechanics workstream.
sources.relevance: Treated gelatin/cellulose film wet tensile comparator, 33 MPa after one-hour hydration; not H2 permeability evidence.
sources.limitation: No transport coefficient transferred from mechanical or water-resistance tests. See mechanics.md for conditions.

sources.title: NIST-JANAF Thermochemical Tables, Water (liquid)
sources.access: Official full table read, 298.15 K row.
sources.limitation: Reference-state splitting work and enthalpy; no biological efficiency or local pressure/temperature correction implied.
